title: Dahibara Aloodum in Cuttack
lead: One bowl, several textures. Leave a pause in the day for a conversation over food.
photo_context: Dahibara-aludam photographed in Cuttack by Subhashish Panigrahi, 2011. A portrait of the dish, not a current vendor or menu.
footline: Follow the bowl. Meet the person serving it.

sections.title: Begin with the bowl
sections.text: Soft lentil fritters in yogurt meet a spicy potato curry: Incredible India describes the combination that gives dahibara-aloodum its contrast. Notice the softer pieces, then the potato and its gravy. Ask how the cook builds their serving; proportions and toppings can change from one kitchen to another.
sections.question: What goes into your version, and how would you suggest trying it?

sections.title: Make a little tasting game
sections.text: Try a small taste of each part before mixing the bowl. Notice softness, spice and contrast, then find the combination you like. Ask for a smaller serving or less chilli if that suits you. These are tasting prompts, not a recipe or a claim that every vendor serves the same preparation.
sections.question: Which taste would bring you back—and what would you ask for next time?

closing: Ask about ingredients, preparation, dietary needs and the price before ordering. Choose a serving and a place to eat that suit you; arrange drinking water and a pause in the day. We have not inspected food stalls, ranked vendors or checked their current menus.
